title: Covered calls sell upside and lag the index on total return
summary: Selling covered calls sells unlimited upside for a limited premium. If your goal is maximum total return, that is the wrong strategy. The speaker cites the CBOE BuyWrite index at about 7.5% a year, the 2% OTM BuyWrite index at just over 10%, and the S&P 500 total return at almost 15%. Covered calls fit income goals, for example in retirement.

params.label: Short call strike
params.help: The 2% OTM BuyWrite index sells calls about 2% above the market.

steps.caption: The index trades at 100. We compare holding it with holding it and selling a 2% out-of-the-money call.
Long stock: upside is unlimited. This is the convexity the covered call seller gives away.
Covered call: the premium adds a little on the downside, but gains stop at the $102 strike.
The difference: you trade unlimited upside for a limited premium. In big rallies the gap is large.
Index data from the clip: BuyWrite about 7.5% a year, 2% OTM BuyWrite just over 10%, S&P 500 almost 15%.

takeaways: A covered call sells unlimited upside for a fixed premium.
By design a covered call program lags the market in strong up markets.
Match the strategy to the goal: covered calls fit income needs, not maximum total return.
caveats: Index return figures are quoted from the video and not checked here.
Stock legs conflict with the owner's options-only rule.
